A CPU cache is a small, fast memory located close to the CPU that stores frequently accessed data to reduce the time required to fetch it from main memory. It operates on the principle of locality, which includes temporal and spatial locality. Temporal locality refers to the tendency of a program to reuse data that has been recently accessed, while spatial locality refers to the tendency to access data that is located near recently accessed data.
